requirements_title: Program Management Support for Financial Systems Modernization
requirement:
The DHS Office of the Chief Financial Officer (OCFO) established the Financial Systems Modernization (FSM) program to oversee Component FSM efforts. The foundational tenets for the FSM programs are:
• Increased business process standardization across Components through efforts to define a common set of financial management business processes and then ensuring Component business process re-engineering and modernization efforts reflect the DHS process standard.
• Implement standard financial data element structures such as the DHS Accounting Classification Structure (ACS) and Common Appropriation Structure (CAS) across Components to standardize reporting and reduce manual reporting processes and inconsistent data.
• Continue to plan and execute financial system modernization projects by migrating Components to a modernized platform or integrating financial systems with asset and procurement management systems that meet Department-wide requirements and financial system and business process standards. FSM projects should also leverage existing infrastructure, shared services, and technologies such as cloud-based solutions to the extent possible, following guidance and lessons learned from previous attempts to integrate DHS Components' financial management systems.
• Lastly, after standardization and modernization has occurred, DHS will work toward consolidating financial operations and transaction processing service centers where cost effective.
•	DHS has established the Enterprise Financial Systems (EFS) office, formerly known as the Joint Program Management Office (JPMO), to lead and manage all aspects of the FSM programs, in partnership with DHS Components. Roles and responsibilities for the EFS are defined in the EFS Charter and other governance documents.

CISA’s Office of the Chief Financial Officer (OCFO) established a Project Management Office (PMO) to manage its FSM initiative at the Component-level. This PMO is comprised of a project manager and systems accountants. It established an FSM Integrated Project Team (IPT) to provide programmatic and functional expertise to manage and support the FSM transition and potential migration. Due to the resource-intensive nature of the Discovery and implementation phases of migration, CISA’s FSM PMO requires programmatic and technical support to assist in the modernization effort.

This requirement provides continued technical, functional, and program management support for CISA’s Financial Systems Modernization (FSM) effort throughout the implementation phase, and preparation for enterprise-wide deployment. Contractor support includes data management and migration support, system integration coordination, and functional expertise necessary to maintain momentum across FSM phases and ensure readiness for transition to a modernized DHS financial management solution. These subject matter experts (SMEs) are critical support roles to ensure financial data integrity, continuity of business processes, and a seamless integration to the unified system approach across the Department.

OBJECTIVE
The objective of the FSM PMO Support is to support CISA OCFO throughout the lifecycle of the FSM Program, in partnership with EFS, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as its financial services provider, and the DHS system integrator, so that the FSM solution is: configured to meet CISA requirements; CISA Financial Data is prepared so that it is able to be migrated to the future solution; CISA users are apprised of the migration and are trained and ready to accept the system upon go-live.
requirements_office: Office of the Chief Financial Officer

requirements_title: Emergency Meals - 2027
requirement:
This requirement supports FEMA’s ability to maintain readiness, replenish Initial Response Resources, and respond rapidly to disasters affecting populations across CONUS, OCONUS, and U.S. territories. The Government requires contractor/s with the capacity and capability to produce, package, and deliver multiple emergency meal types in support of FEMA’s disaster response missions. Mandatory meal types include Survivor Daily Rations (vegetarian and meat options), while optional meal types include Reduced Sodium Meals, Commercial Meals, and Short Shelf-Life Meals. Upon delivery the meals (excluding the Short Shelf-life meals) shall have a minimum of 36 months shelf life remaining; the Short Shelf-life meals shall have between 9-36 months remaining upon delivery. 
During steady state operations, the contractor shall be capable of delivering the required meal types within 30 days of contract award for CONUS locations and within 45 days of contract award for OCONUS locations. During disaster response operations, the contractor shall be capable of delivering meals within 72 hours for CONUS and 96 hours for OCONUS, ensuring rapid mobilization and sustained support during emergent events.  The contractor shall support delivery throughout all 48 Continental United States (CONUS), Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS), and all U.S. territories. The resulting Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract will consist of one (1) twelve-month base year and four (4) twelve-month option years.

requirement: The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) is authorized under Section 408 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 5174), as amended, to provide Direct Assistance to eligible disaster survivors. As part of its emergency response mission, FEMA provides Transportable Temporary Housing Units (TTHUs). The TTHUs include standard household Baths & Showers. FEMA ensures that all eligible survivors have equal access to Direct Assistance in accordance with the Uniform Federal Accessibility Standards (UFAS) and the Architectural Barriers Act Accessibility Standards (ABAAS), as applicable. To accommodate eligible survivors who require accessible bathing facilities, FEMA retrofits Temporary Housing Units (TTHUs), including Manufactured Housing Units (MHUs), in the field with roll-in showers and transfer tubs when needed to meet a survivor’s requirements.  FEMA has a requirement for a variety "bestbath" brand name or equivalent retro fit showers and accessories installation kits.

naics: 541611 - Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
requirements_title: Risk Methodology and Programmatic Support
requirement: The mission of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA)/Grant Programs Directorate (GPD)/Homeland Security Programs Division (HSPD) is to effectively develop and administer FEMA’s preparedness grant programs which aim to help improve the capacity of state, local and tribal entities to prevent, prepare for, respond to, and recover from natural and manmade hazards, including acts of terrorism. HSPD accomplishes this mission by developing and administering numerous grant programs in close concert with Federal, state, local, tribal, nonprofit, and private stakeholder consultation. HSPD supports the grant process of allocating grant funding to numerous grant programs by developing a comprehensive risk methodology that is used to inform grant allocation decisions. In managing its risk methodology, GPD evaluates threat, vulnerability, and consequence factors to determine the relative risk of states, territories, large urban areas, and tribal nations. GPD is also required to ensure that its efforts support the requirements of the Homeland Security Act of 2002, as amended, as well as DHS and FEMA senior leadership priorities. It is also imperative that GPD works closely with stakeholders internal to GPD, FEMA, and DHS and with stakeholders external to FEMA including state and local first responder communities, as well as private sector partners. DHS program offices that support the grant programs are: the Transportation Security Administration and the United States Coast Guard; DHS components that work with risk data such as the Office of Intelligence and Analysis (I&A), Office of Operations Coordination/Special Events Program, and the National Risk Management Center; Custom and Border Patrol, and other public/private entities that own and/or manage sources of risk data. The activities under this Performance Work Statement are intended to analyze the relative risk of states/territories, and the 100 most populous Metropolitan Statistical Areas in the United States for the purpose of informing allocations under the GPD preparedness grant programs. Risk Methodology and Programmatic Support will provide HSPD with the services necessary to support the development of risk methodologies used to inform grant funding and analytics measuring the preparedness grants for states, territories, urban areas, ports, and transit system. The Contractor will be part of an integrated team, participating with federal employees and other Contractors to support GPD’s strategic and tactical objectives. The Contractor shall provide all necessary support services to meet the tasks and deliverables defined in the following functional project areas: -Support the current Grant Risk Methodologies -Future risk strategies development -Programmatic monitoring and oversight. The Contractor shall provide solutions, options, and recommendations to the Government through a review and approval process. The Government will determine all courses of action for implementation, and the Contractor will assist in the development project implementation plans on a timeline schedule on request.

requirement: FEMA Region IX’s Area of Response (AOR) includes the Pacific Basin, specifically Guam, American Samoa, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI). FEMA employees regularly proceed on official travel to this AOR to provide support and assistance. requirement:
TSA’s current financial system is the Financial System Modernization Solution (FSMS), which is a suite of applications that includes Oracle Federal Financials (OFF), Sunflower Assets (SA) and Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM). FSMS also integrates with TSA feeder systems which automate certain business processes, such as Concur Government Edition (CONCURGOV which is the employee travel management system) and MarkView (for invoice imaging and approval workflow). In addition to these feeder systems, TSA uses the National Finance Center (NFC), a service-based organization to process payroll from the U.S. Treasury Department and distribute payment to TSA employees. To reflect payroll transactions in FSMS, the NFC payroll files are downloaded and processed on a bi-weekly basis to update the FSMS general ledger. These systems integrate with FSMS to ensure that all financial transactions are properly posted to the general ledger. TSA supports the TFDW (an Oracle Data warehouse) utilizing Oracle Business Intelligence Applications (OBIA) /Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition (OBIEE) /Oracle Data Integrator (ODI)/ Oracle Application Express (APEX) that is hosted in the Amazon Web Service (AWS) Cloud by DHS. TSA provides Database Administration (DBA), OBIA/OBIEE development/maintenance/enhancements to a suite of business Dashboards and Reports for 600 users.

TSA requires a Contractor to support the oversight of the financial systems service provider and provide functional and business intelligence (BI) support to the TSA financial systems user community. Effective systems management and associated services will facilitate successful accomplishment of overall financial management objectives.

TSA does not operate or maintain the production systems; nor does TSA perform system development work to modify the financial systems (those are our service provider’s responsibilities). TSA develops BI reports and administers the OBIA/OBIEE/ODI/APEX environments to support the TSA user community. The principal purpose of the solicited service is for the Contractor to provide financial management systems functional and BI support. The solicited services will be performed primarily within the TSA Chief Finance Office (CFO) and require a unique combination of functional and technical expertise in a Federal financial management system environment with a heavy emphasis on the Federal financial, accounting, and financial systems functional expertise. Specifically, TSA requires Contractor support to: 1. Provide overall project and task order management support; 2. Provide overall financial systems implementation support services and operations and maintenance which include, but are not limited to, general IT control activities, financial systems functional support, and travel system support; and 3. Provide Data Warehouse and Oracle BI Support, which include overall Data Warehouse/BI Support Activities, Project Lead and BI Architect Support, DBA Support, BI/OBIA Administration Support, and BI Development Support.

requirements_title: National Hazardous Materials Management & Disposal Services (VAP)
requirement:
Prior to passage of the Aviation and Transportation Security Act (ATSA), Pub.L. 107 71, the air carriers were responsible for the screening of commercial air carrier passengers.  They also were responsible for the collection and disposition of all prohibited items, including hazardous materials.  With the passage of ATSA, TSA became responsible for the screening of these passengers.  49 U.S.C. §44901(a).  

As a result, TSA determined that it had the legal responsibility to accept prohibited and hazardous items abandoned by passengers at security checkpoints.  Having accepted the property, TSA is legally liable for the disposition of abandoned or forfeited personal property.  Hazardous materials, if not otherwise donated per 41 CFR 101-42.304, must be disposed of in accordance with Federal and state laws and regulations.  42 U.S.C. §6901 et seq.

In 2003, TSA issued the National Voluntarily Abandoned Property and Hazardous Material Disposal Contract to assist with the management, disposition and disposal of the prohibited and hazardous items abandoned by passengers at security checkpoints.  In April 2005, TSA added lighters to the prohibited item list as directed by Congress in the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004. Liquids, Gels, and Aerosols (LGA) were also added to the prohibited list in August 2006 while lighters were removed from the prohibited list in August 2007.  As a result, the type and amount of hazardous items abandoned by passengers at security checkpoints have changed and increased in quantity since April 2005.

TSA requires a Contractor to provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, vehicles, supervision, and other items and services necessary to perform hazard materials management and disposal for approximately 450 airport locations (and ancillary TSA offices when necessary).  The number of airports and airport locations is subject to change throughout the life of any resultant contract depending on privatization and Federalization decisions, new airports opening, the operation of seasonal airports or reorganizations that affect TSA operations.  Services shall be performed for all airports/collections areas.  The Contractor must meet or exceed all Federal, State, and local regulations.

To support this, the TSA Employee Parking Assistance Program (EPAP) provides a simplified means for TSA to subsidize parking, the cost of which is a recurring concern among the workforce, which reduces administrative burden on TSA. requirements_title: Operations and Maintenance (O&M) Services for the TSIF and Freedom Center
requirement:
The Transportation Security Administration System Integration Facility (TSIF) is in Arlington, VA at the Reagan Washington National Airport.  It is a 128,000 sq. ft. two story building equipped with three elevators.  The TSIF building was purchased by TSA from the United States Postal Office in October 2010 and is situated on Metropolitan Washington Airport Authority (MWAA) property. The operations and maintenance (O&M) of the building’s exterior infrastructure (façade, windows, and roof), parking lot paving and striping, ground floor baggage handling equipment, and sidewalk maintenance (excluding snow removal) are managed by the Building Property Manager and are excluded from the scope of this Task Order. 

The Freedom Center is housed in Herndon, VA and consists of 104,014 rentable square feet (103,502 usable square feet per BOMA standards) in a single-story building.  The Freedom Center (FC) was established in response to the direction provided by the National Strategy for Combating Terrorism, as part of the President’s Management Strategy.  Operational since July 2003, the Freedom Center serves as TSA’s 24/7 coordination center for transportation security-related operations, incidents, or crises for TSA within the Department of Homeland Security.  It integrates real-time intelligence and operational information, ensuring unity of command and action in preventing and responding to terrorist-related incidents across all transportation modes (maritime, land, and aviation).

TSA requires complete operations and maintenance services for the above-referenced facilities. The Contractor shall ensure all required project management, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, grounds maintenance, and housekeeping (including janitorial, custodial, equipment and systems testing/inspection, preventive/predictive maintenance, corrective maintenance/repair, 24/7/365 operations, and emergency services) are performed to provide a safe and comfortable environment for building occupants. Preventive maintenance service calls must meet or exceed commercial standards. All tasks must comply with applicable codes, laws, regulations, and policies at all levels. Services must be provided 24/7 for the Freedom Center and 5 days per week for the TSIF facility.

TSA anticipates issuing a contract for these services under the AbilityOne Program.

requirements_title: Technical Support Services
requirement:
The United States Coast Guard (USCG) Aviation Logistics Center (ALC) provides centralized logistics support for all USCG aviation missions. As the sole industrial complex for USCG aviation, ALC provides: depot level maintenance, engineering, supply, procurement, acquisition, and information services.  ALC's mission supports twenty five (25) USCG aviation units that operate approximately two hundred (200) aircraft.  These air stations are located throughout the continental United States, Alaska, Hawaii, and Puerto Rico. Additionally, ALC supports USCG Headquarters, Aviation Technical Training Center (ATTC), and USCG Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC).  Technical Support Services are required to support the mission of ALC in various divisions: Engineering Services Division (ESD), Operational Division (OPS), Medium Range Surveillance (MRS), Medium Range Recovery (MRR), Long Range Surveillance (LRS), Safety and Environmental Health Office (SEHO), Aviation Projects and Acquisitions Center (APAC).  Other ALC divisions may be added at a later date.
The required services generally include, but are not limited to:
•	Technical Support
•	System Integration Support
•	Modification Support
•	Field Services Technical Support
•	Management Support
•	Safety
•	Environmental Science and Protection

This will be a full-set aside using Oasis+ and the group will Set Aside for Women Owned Small Business.

This software is integrated with other IBM products to maintain requirements traceability for ALMIS subsystems, Coast Guard - Logistics Information Management System (CG-LIMS), and other ALC utilized applications. naics: 334511 - Search, Detection, Navigation, Guidance, Aeronautical, and Nautical System and Instrument Manufactur
requirements_title: Scalable Integrated Navigation System Generation 2 (SINS-2) Follow-on
requirement:
Background and Purpose:
The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) requires a follow-on Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract to procure next-generation Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) marine navigation systems. This effort is the successor to the Scalable Integrated Navigation System 2 (SINS-2) program (Contract HSCG44-17-D-170005) and aims to recapitalize and modernize the standardized electronic navigation suites across the USCG's diverse fleet of cutters and boats.
Scope of Work:
This contract is for hardware and associated chart subscriptions; installation and maintenance will be handled via separate actions. The contractor shall provide a scalable suite of COTS marine electronics that are interconnected via a NMEA 2000 compliant backbone. The core components include, but are not limited to: Multifunction Displays (MFDs) in various sizes (e.g., 4-6", 7-8", 10-12"), Radome and Open Array radar systems, GPS receivers, depth sounders with multiple transducer options, and heading sensors. The scope also requires the provision of updated electronic navigation charts for all procured systems. All hardware must meet the ruggedization and EMI/RFI standards outlined in IEC 60945.
Technical and Cybersecurity Requirements:
The system must be interoperable with existing USCG infrastructure, including the capability to process and display Encrypted Automatic Identification System (EAIS) data as specified in the EAIS Interface Design Description (IDD). All procured hardware, firmware, and software must adhere to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) cybersecurity directives and Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) protocols. The contractor must also have a robust obsolescence management plan, providing form, fit, and function replacements for components with a minimum of 18 months' notice.
Period of Performance and Scalability:
The anticipated Period of Performance is a two-year base period with eight one-year option periods, allowing for a total of ten years. The contract must be highly scalable to ensure continuous lifecycle support for the current fleet and to serve as a strategic bridge to future navigation system technologies, mitigating any potential fielding delays.
apfs_coordinator_office: C5I C3 Contract Operations Division 3 (APFS Coordinator)

requirements_title: Illicit Drug Trace Detection
requirement:
The United States Coast Guard’s (USCG) maritime law enforcement mission includes countering illicit narcotic trafficking. Maritime law enforcement encompasses armed intervention by uniformed Coast Guard personnel, conducted both aboard vessels and at facilities ashore, to detect and suppress violations of applicable law. 
To support this critical mission, USCG units are authorized to conduct Contraband Detection Activities (CDA) to determine the presence of contraband. CDA involves the use of organic, mechanical, or chemical devices that sample or examine the air or physical surfaces to detect narcotics or explosives. The purpose of this project is to acquire and field advanced Narcotic Trace Detection (NTD) devices to fulfill this operational CDA requirement.
apfs_coordinator_office: C5I C2 Contract Operations Division 2 (APFS Coordinator)

This contract covers four primary functions:

requirements_title: United States Coast Guard (USCG) Response Boat – Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
requirement:
The Response Boat – Small Third Generation (RB-S III) represents the USCG's recapitalization of the 29-foot Response Boat-Small (RB-S II). The RB-S fleet consists of approximately 400 boats designed for a 15-year service life, with a top speed exceeding 40 knots, and exhibiting exceptional maneuverability. As the USCG’s primary asset for Search and Rescue (SAR), Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security (PWCS), and Law Enforcement (LE) missions in coastal areas, the RB-S needs to be capable of towing vessels up to 10 tons displacement. The RB-S III will maintain the primary mission requirements of its predecessor, with potential expanded roles in Drug Interdiction (DI) and Migrant Interdiction (MI) operations. The USCG plans to acquire up to 400 boats, with the option for other Government agencies to order up to 100 additional modified variants. In addition to the boats and trailers, the program will include delivery of the following support elements: 

Technical Data: Drawings, 3D models, Bill of Material (BOM), and commercial manuals to support the development of maintenance instructions. 
Interim Contractor Logistics Support (ICLS):  ICLS (labor and material) to sustain the boats until organic Coast Guard Support has been established. 
Spares: Initial provisioning spares for the first year of operation and system insurance spares (e.g., fenders, spare engines). 

The USCG plans to award up to four (4) contracts in FY2027, each with a minimum order quantity of one (1) boat, and order one (1) boat from each contract. These boats will be operated to verify the delivered boats align with the previously submitted and evaluated paper proposals. At the conclusion of this process, a single boat builder will be selected to produce the RB-S III fleet.

All information in this forecast is for planning purposes only and is subject to change pending approval of the acquisition strategy and supporting acquisition documents. This forecast does not constitute a solicitation, presolicitation notice, or Government commitment.

Its purpose is to reduce attrition, increase operational capability, and provide evidence-based performance decisions. The database system must generate configurable analytical reports and rollups based on end-user input, capture human attributes related to training objectives, and retrieve historical data to inform assessment or training criteria changes.
The software application must be compatible with USCG-approved mobile devices and the Non-classified Internet Protocol Router (NIPR) network, allowing instructors to access forms, evaluations, and training materials efficiently. It must include features such as an Automatic Feedback Tool (AFT) to provide tailored feedback based on student performance, a Package Builder for organizing student files, and compatibility with CG Cloud infrastructure for data storage and handling. The system must comply with Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and USCG security standards, Defense Information Assurance Certification Accreditation, and Section 508 accessibility requirements.
The Contractor shall provide licensing for approximately 750 students and 150 instructors/staff, maintain and update the software, address bugs, and ensure compatibility with technological advancements. Software updates must support curriculum changes, enhance security, and maintain accreditation. The contract must provide scalability for additional licenses, modules, or convenings as operational needs evolve, with flexibility to meet surge training demands within the contract's period of performance.

requirements_title: Continuous Synopsis Record
requirement:
This contract is essential to ensure the U.S. Coast Guard fulfills international maritime security obligations under the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) by maintaining accurate Continuous Synopsis Records (CSR) for the U.S. flag fleet.  Under the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS), the United States is legally obligated to maintain an up-to-date Continuous Synopsis Record (CSR) for all applicable vessels. Executing this contract ensures the U.S. Coast Guard remains compliant with these binding international maritime safety and security standards. 

A failure to maintain these records degrades our ability to monitor maritime threats and compromises international security protocols. The administrative bandwidth required to process, update, and manage these records across the fleet is substantial.  Dedicated contractor support is required to execute this essential administrative function. Without this contract, CG-CVC will lack the necessary administrative capacity to process CSRs in a timely manner. This would result in international non-compliance, potential delays or detentions of U.S. flagged vessels in foreign ports, and a degraded posture in global maritime security tracking.

requirements_title: USCGC HEALY Steering Control System
requirement:
The Coast Guard is planning to replace the steering control system on CGC HEALY located in Seattle, Washington.  The existing steering control system is configured such that rudder angle is controlled from the following helm locations: Main bridge station, (4) secondary conning stations and the steering gear room steering console.  The control system is a combination of electrical and hydraulic equipment with analog backup methods as a redundant fail-safe solution.  All system components and sub-systems (e.g. Rudder Servo Amplifier, Rudder Repeat Back, Rudder Angle Transmitter, and Steering Failure Alarm Panel) shall be replaced with a commercial of the shelf (COTS) in-kind or upgraded technical solution to prevent loss of capabilities. 
The replacement system must interface with existing auxiliary and navigation systems as defined in the Statement of Work, Coast Guard technical manuals, electrical schematics and drawings.  No proprietary information of the incumbent steering control system will be provided except for the interfacing systems such as electro-hydraulic steering gear and navigation system communications protocols.
Technical solutions for replacement steering control system must meet the design and safety requirements of 46 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Subparts 58, 111, and 113; the International Maritime Organization (IMO) Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS); and the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS). 
The Vendor shall supply Provisioning Technical Data (PTD) that includes certified technical manuals and drawings describing the steering system control system to the United States Coast Guard (USCG) with sufficient information to produce installation drawings.  The Vendor shall also supply Engineering Data for Provisioning (EDFP) on the system and components concurrent with the delivery of the equipment to allow the USCG to produce maintenance procedure cards (MPCs) and other logistical support documentation. Engineering data shall also include the PLC code (where applicable) for operation of the system.  The Vendor shall provide on-site technical support for training, system testing, commissioning, and certification.  The Vendor shall provide maintenance parts lists and a recommended onboard repair parts (OBRP) list for all components.

requirements_title: USCGC HEALY (WAGB-20) Service Life Extension Program Integrated Power Plant system upgrades
requirement:
The Coast Guard is planning to conduct specific sub-system recapitalizations in support of the CGC HEALY Service Life Extension Program (SLEP) from FY2027 to FY 2031. A number of these system recapitalizations require integration and tie-in to the existing Integrated Power Plant (IPP) system. The existing IPP system is comprised of the Central Power Plant (common bus electric propulsion and auxiliary power generation systems) and selected components/systems in the auxiliary machinery plant, which is maintained/managed by a separate services contract. 

This acquisition is a multi-year contract with the scope focusing on the integration of the recapitalized sub-systems into the IPP system. The sub-systems intended to be recapitalized currently include: the Science Sea Water System Pump and Cyclone Separator, Steering Control System Components, Sanitary System Components, Over-the-Side Weight Handling System, Deaerating Feedwater Tanks, and the Bow Thruster. The IPP system is proprietary and the USCG intends to award to a sole source for this acquisition to the Original Equipment Manufacturer. The Vendor shall provide on-site technical support for training, system testing, commissioning, and certification. The Vendor shall provide maintenance parts lists and a recommended onboard repair parts (OBRP) list for all components.

requirements_title: USCGC HEALY (WAGB-20) Service Life Extension Program Anchor Handling and Controls Parts Procurement
requirement: The Coast Guard is planning to procure two new anchor windlasses assemblies and their associated major spare part sub-assemblies to replace the obsolete anchor windlasses on USCGC HEALY located in Seattle, Washington.  The HEALY requires two anchor windlass assemblies, one configured for port and one configured for starboard installation. The assemblies shall include the complete mechanical assembly including the capstan head, gypsy head, gearcase, mechanical/hydraulic brakes, hydraulic motor, brake control stands, centralized greasing system and interconnecting components. This procurement does not include installation of the equipment but does include limited technical support by the Contractor to the United States Coast Guard (USCG) to ensure that the equipment is installed correctly and functions correctly.  The anchor windlasses must meet the design and safety requirements of 46 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Subparts 58, 111, and 113; the International Maritime Organization (IMO) Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS); and the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS). The Vendor shall supply Provisioning Technical Data (PTD) that includes certified technical manuals and drawings describing the system controls to the United States Coast Guard (USCG) with sufficient information to produce installation drawings. The Vendor shall also supply Engineering Data for Provisioning (EDFP) on the system and components concurrent with the delivery of the equipment to allow the USCG to produce maintenance procedure cards (MPCs) and other logistical support documentation. Engineering data shall also include the PLC code (where applicable) for operation of the system. The Vendor shall conduct a factory acceptance test of the system and shall provide on-site technical support for training, system testing, commissioning, and certification. The Vendor shall provide a maintenance parts lists and a recommended onboard repair parts (OBRP) list for all components.

requirements_title: Design & Installation of Replacement Ship's Service and Emergency Switchboard for the US Coast Guard 154 WPC Class Cutter (Hulls 1101 through 1138)
requirement:
Earlier 154 WPC class cutters, also known as the USCG Fast Response Cutter (FRC), utilize Ship’s Service and Emergency Switchboards designed and built by RAACI (Robichaux Automation and Control, Inc.). These are applicable to all Phase 1 cutters (Hulls 1101 thru 1132) and early Phase 2 cutters (Hulls 1133 thru 1138). These switchboards utilize Woodard EasyGen 3200 series controllers and Siemens 3VL circuit breakers and PLCs.  The RAACI switchboards use older technology that is currently experiencing obsolescence and part supply issues. Hulls 1139 and up utilize switchboards designed and built by Point Eight Power, incorporated via an Engineering Change Proposal through the acquisition program. To improve commonality of systems and address obsolescence within the FRC fleet, the U.S. Coast Guard seeks to retrofit Hulls 1101 through 1138 with Point Eight Power switchboards. This requirement is a non-personal services contract to provide all labor, materials, services, equipment, supplies, power, accessories and facilities to upgrade the Ship’s Service and Emergency Generator Switchboards on the United States Coast Guard (USCG) 154’ Sentinel Class (154 WPC) cutters, Hulls 1101 through 1138.

Place of Performance: Design efforts will be accomplished at the Contractor's facility. Installations onboard two cutters (TBD) will be accomplished either at vessels homeport or during a shipyard availability.

requirements_title: USCGC ALEX HALEY Switchboard Replacement
requirement: The 282-FT USCGC ALEX HALEY (WMEC-39) Ship Service Switchboards are no longer supportable and require replacement. This project entails the replacement of the ship's service switchboards through a comprehensive three-phase process covering design, fabrication, and installation support. The new 450 VAC, three-phase switchboard must adhere to strict dimensional constraints, with a maximum size of 192 inches in length, 25.25 inches in depth, and 81 inches in height, and must be built to UL 891 and IEEE 45 standards. Designed for a marine environment, it will consist of four separable sections to facilitate rigging and installation and must withstand up to 45° rolls and 10° pitch. Additionally, the vendor will be required to perform critical electrical system analyses, including studies on fault currents, protective device coordination, arc flash, and failure modes.

requirements_title: MIDGETT NR2 Caterpillar (CAT) Ship Service Diesel Generator, Engine Major Overhaul
requirement:
CGC MIDGETT #2 SSDG experienced high crankcase pressure with oil/smoke/vapor protruding from lube oil dipstick ports and crankcase vents. Ships Force attempted minor dynamic troubleshooting, but vapor generation was too rapid to continue operation of the engine. The SSDG was tagged out and opened and remained open for further investigation work and repairs. The cutter has submitted DISCREP #26048 requesting Depot Level assistance from LREPL. 

The contractor must execute the Major Overhaul listed in TP 14025 (SMCS Code 7595-020-MJ). 

The Contractor may be directed to renew the Crankshaft.

Following crankcase obstruction verification, the Contractor may be directed to perform a Hot Lube Oil Flush of the engine and ancillary equipment.

requirements_title: Manufacture and Delivery of Steel Foam Filled River Buoys
requirement:
This requirement is for the manufacture and delivery of steel foamfilled
river buoys for United States Coast Guard (USCG) Waterway Operations
Product Line (WOPL) used by Aids to Navigation (ATON) units across the United
States. Title 14 of the United States Code authorizes the USCG to maintain
ATON buoys to guide mariners in the navigable waters of the United States. The
type of buoy that is specifically used in the rivers of the Midwest is known as a
"river buoy." River buoys are continually lost or destroyed on station through
collisions with passing vessels, extreme weather conditions, or simply through
wear and tear in the harsh marine environment. These buoys must therefore be
replaced in large numbers. On average, about three-quarters of all river buoys
deployed on station are replaced annually. There is a need to establish a
contract for the manufacture and delivery of river buoys to meet the USCG's
operational requirements for these aids.

These spaces are essential for maintaining professionalism and privacy while conducting interviews and meetings crucial for recruitment efforts. Recruiters in detached locations also have the responsibility of assessing the need for permanent recruitment presence. Providing them with dedicated workspaces supports day-to-day activities and aids in evaluating the necessity for long-term recruitment resources. The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is procuring Janitorial Services for USCG Base Borinquen (including the USCG Exchange) Aguadilla, PR.

requirements_title: Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) System
requirement: The U.S. Secret Service Police force has a need for an integrated next-generation Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) system and real-time situational awareness platform.  The system will enable secure, interoperable communications, advanced analytics, asset tracking, and mobile support for field personnel, all of which are essential for effective incident management and response coordination. The CAD system needs to have the following characteristics: assistive AI, and advanced geospatial capabilities in a single, unified solution. The system will need to support both cloud SaaS and on-premises deployments, ensuring flexibility and compliance with US Secret Service Police security and infrastructure needs. Additionally, the system will need to have a proven record of interoperability with key regional partners in the National Capital Region (NCR) like Arlington County PD, Fairfax County PD, and the District of Columbia Office of Unified Communications to ensure seamless collaboration during joint operations and large-scale events, while maintaining each agencies unique policies, workflows, permissions and business rules configured to meet their individual needs.

requirement:
This requirement is for contractor support to provide three Agile-driven teams to deliver program management, risk management, and knowledge management services for the Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP)systems and programs. The Contractor will support performance measurement, process improvement, data analytics, requirements management, and business case development for SEVP operations. Responsibilities include developing and maintaining risk management plans for the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) Programs Section and System Management Unit. The Contractor support team will coordinate risk reviews, provide independent risk assessments, and manage risk inventories and mitigation strategies. Additionally, the Contractor team will support the operational management of program documentation and knowledge libraries within the SEVP Assessment Management System (SEVPAMS), ensuring proper version control and metadata management. Strategic planning and administrative support will be provided to facilitate efficient operations, compliance with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) privacy and information assurance policies, and continuous improvement of SEVP systems and processes. The scope excludes software development and focuses on management, administration, and support functions.

Based on the market research results, this requirement will be solicited as a 100% Small Business Set Aside via NAICS 541611 in accordance with the procedures at  RFO FAR Subpart 8.4, Ordering under the Federal Supply Schedule, and GSAR 538.71, Federal Supply Schedule Ordering Procedures.

requirements_title: On-Site Compliance Assessment Support Services for ICE 287(g) Public Safety Partnership Division
requirement:
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) seeks contractor support to conduct approximately 1,000 comprehensive, on-site compliance assessments over the course of one year of Law Enforcement Partner (LEP) agencies participating in the ICE 287(g) program under the Task Force Model (TFM) and Warrant Service Officer (WSO) Model. The contractor will provide qualified compliance assessment personnel or teams to travel to LEP facilities, perform detailed operational and programmatic reviews, collect and analyze data, conduct interviews, and prepare findings and compliance reports for ICE ERO. Contractor personnel will work with the appropriate ICE ERO Field Office to facilitate corrective action plans and submit final reports.

The Contractor shall furnish all personnel, supervision, equipment, and materials necessary to conduct approximately 1,000 on-site compliance assessments per year of LEP agencies under the TFM and WSO models. The Contractor will be responsible for all aspects of the compliance assessment process, including pre-assessment planning, on-site activities, data collection, interviews, post-assessment analysis, and reporting.

Contract services will include but are not limited to pre-assessment planning, coordination with partner agencies, document review, on-site assessments, interviews, credential reviews, operational observances, report preparation, corrective action recommendations, and final report submission.

The total period of performance for this effort is 36 months comprised of one 12-month base period of performance beginning on the date of contract award and one 2-year option period exercisable at the Government’s discretion. 

The Contractor shall ensure adequate contracted staffing to meet the operational requirements of this contract, and provide qualified, experienced personnel.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) is responsible for leading DHS’ Digital Transformation by providing enterprise information technology (IT) services, technical architectural planning, and oversight of IT portfolios.  The OCIO strengthens cybersecurity, IT acquisition, IT security, and executive oversight, and promotes the use of standardized, reusable IT solutions within a unified framework for managing DHS IT investments.

The OCIO seeks to provide innovative business solutions, lower costs through shared services, and reduce time to delivery for new capabilities. As the foundation for customer-centric service delivery, OCIO establishes a secure utility computing environment where innovation, re-use, efficiency, and quality are core principles.  

The OCIO supports both new mission requirements and modernization efforts, including: 

Leveraging new technology 

Replacing manual, inefficient processes with automation 

Integrating data across DHS for advanced analytics and improved decision-making 

The OCIO also supports strategic data management to ensure DHS acquires, ingests, generates, maintains, manages, governs, stores, and shares data in an efficient and mission-focused manner.  This will improve the Department’s data posture, providing clear leadership, and a mechanism for effective strategic prioritization and management of DHS enterprise data.

requirements_title: Card Upgrade and Redesign of Equipment (CURE)
requirement:
The Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), requires a comprehensive solution for the production and personalization of secure identification cards under the Card Upgrade and Refresh of Equipment (CURE) program. The requirement includes supporting the USCIS Office of Intake and Document Production, Document Management Division, in delivering a redesigned card and card production system for Permanent Resident Cards (PRC) and Employment Authorization Document (EAD) cards at the Corbin, Kentucky and Lee’s Summit, Missouri production facilities.

The requirement includes the design and high-volume manufacturing of a new secure card constructed of 100% polycarbonate with embedded Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) and metallized optically variable devices. The card design must be configurable for multiple immigration benefit types and future document types, allowing for updates to artwork, color schemes, and mastheads. Fulfillment of the requirement includes providing card stock storage and a card personalization solution capable of producing both the new and legacy PRC and EAD cards until legacy stock is depleted.

The requirement includes installation and ongoing maintenance of the card personalization system, development of an operator user interface, integration with existing USCIS information systems, and support for system acceptance and user acceptance testing. The solution must include user training and technical support. The system must support high-volume production, scalable to at least ten million cards per year per site, and provide redundancy to meet continuity of operations requirements.

All solutions and services must comply with Department of Homeland Security Enterprise Architecture policies, technical reference models, and data management standards. Hardware and software maintenance must be provided as well as system upgrades, consumables management, and operational support for both production sites. The system must include automated and manual quality assurance, inventory management, card tracking, and reporting capabilities. Reports must cover inventory, card production, scanning issues, rejected cards, work in progress, and other operational metrics.

The requirement includes delivery of all required documentation, including project management plans, system design documents, training materials, interface control agreements, supply chain risk management plans, and system transition plans. All personnel must meet security and background investigation requirements for access to sensitive but unclassified information and government facilities. Fulfillment of the requirement includes equipment delivery, installation, integration, and testing.

requirement:
USCIS has a requirement for Enterprise Gateway and Integration Services (EGIS) III. requirements_title: Thales FY27
requirement: USCIS has a requirement to obtain the software license renewal for Thales Device HSM (Hardware Security Module) as a Service which is a key component of the overall device certificate automation project. An HSM is a specialized physical device designed to securely store and manage digital keys, cryptographic operations, and sensitive information. They provide a high level of protection for cryptographic processes and serve as a secure foundation for various security applications. Additionally, they offer a range of features including key generation, storage and protection, cryptographic operations (such as encryption and decryption), secure key exchange, and digital signatures. By employing tamper-resistant hardware and robust security mechanisms, HSMs help safeguard sensitive data and cryptographic keys from unauthorized access and tampering attempts. They also support compliance with regulatory standards and provide a trusted platform for building secure systems.

requirements_title: Gigamon FY27
requirement: USCIS is looking to renew the Gigamon software license which is a platform that meets the following requirements. Compliant Deployment Model: The network TAPs must be on-premises physical devices as they are required to be placed in-line of the physical network cables. The network TAPs must support private cloud deployment to be placed in-line with USCIS cloud deployed instances. Supportability: The network TAPs must offer active TAPs to amplify and mirror network traffic. The network TAPs must be able to support copper and fiber optic network traffic. The network TAPs vendor must offer a passive TAP to limit interference with network traffic. The network TAP must support up to 100GB bandwidth of network traffic. Filtering: The network TAP must support port mirroring and aggregation. The network TAP must be able to filter on source and destination IP addresses, port numbers, protocol, VLAN, MAC address, and content. The network TAP should be able to filter on encrypted SSL/TLS traffic. Management: The network TAP must be able to be managed from remote locations and support centralized management. Native OCSF Support: The TAP system must support sending data compliant with the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF).

requirements_title: National Benefits Center (NBC) Records Operation Contract (ROC)
requirement:
"In support of the processing of applications and petitions for adjudication of immigration benefits, the National Benefits Center (NBC) Records Operations Contract (ROC) provides non-inherently Governmental services that encompass a wide range of pre-processing activities in order to accomplish the mission-essential functions required at the NBC. The primary functions of this contract include, but are not limited to, Correspondence Management (e.g., courier services, file and mail management, and monetary instrument handling); Case Preparation (assembly of various applications or petitions in accordance with USCIS policies and procedures); File Control and Maintenance (e.g., file merging, A-File creation, and case updates); Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) scanning (the scanning of all documents within a file(s) and the upload into the designated FOIA system); and Program Management.  NBC ROC services are provided at the NBC locations in Lee's Summit, MO and Overland Park, KS.  

NBC's mission is to create and support the centralization of the pre-processing required to support the Field Offices under the Field Office Directorate (FOD). NBC ROC supports the following mission critical functions: (1) Mail, File & Data Entry/scan support for over 2.5 million applications annually (2) Support for Freedom of Information Act requests (3) Large-scale file room operations, reducing the need for records support staff and space at field offices (4) Pre-processing activities for over 3 million applications and petitions annually (5) Case preparation and review for approx. 800,000 Adjustment of Status applications (6) Initiation of requests for initial evidence for approx. 300,000 Adjustment of Status applications annually (7) Manual Name Harvesting for security checks, saving officer resources and improving processing times (8) Tracking and monitoring of case work and adjudication-ready cases (9) Management of workflows for over 1 million records adjudicated at the NBC."

requirements_title: Recapitalize CG Station Freeport
requirement:
The U.S. Coast Guard is soliciting proposals for the Coast Guard Station Freeport Recapitalization project. This project entails the design and construction of a new, hurricane-resilient Coast Guard Station in Freeport, TX, to replace facilities severely damaged by Hurricane Beryl. The scope includes constructing a 20,635 GSF purpose-built facility, including an attached drive-through boat maintenance facility, featuring hurricane-resistant design elements such as elevation above the 100-year base flood elevation and open/breakaway ground floor walls. The facility will incorporate elevators, a building information system, fire protection and alarm systems, and an emergency power system of up to 1,000 kW capable of sustaining mission operations for at least 10 days following major storm events. 

Supporting infrastructure requirements encompass utilities, mechanical systems (including relocation of existing rescue equipment), a boat bay hoist, paving, walks, curbs, gutters, site improvements, and a new resilient small boat storage structure. Pier upgrades are also required, including new fuel dispensers and elevated shore-side transformers. The existing building and remaining portions of the small boat storage structure will be demolished, and temporary facilities must be provided during construction. The new facility will be constructed on the existing site. Bidders must demonstrate experience in hurricane-resistant construction, coastal construction, and complex utility upgrades.

requirements_title: M&R Bldg 205 SSO Locker
requirement:
The SSO Locker Building (Bldg. 205) serves as the sole ready gear locker/wet room facility at Sector New York. The building is a single story 5291 SF prefabricated modular structure constructed in 2006 on a concrete block foundation with a flat roof and surrounded by a faux brick skirt. The building contains Male and Female locker rooms, heads, wet rooms and storage spaces. The roof has numerous leaks. The fire alarm system no longer functions (due to water intrusion) and the building lacks emergency egress signs and modern lighting. The building (essentially a large locker room/head) is not ventilated (non-code compliant construction) and contains a continuous strong musty odor. The ½” thick exterior brick facade architectural panels are peeling away from the building. The wooden access staircases and doors are rotting. The vinyl flooring has rips and gashes throughout caused by the flexing of the poorly supported under flooring. 

SCOPE:
Summary: This project will replace the roof and façade, replace the entryways, add ventilation, replace the fire alarm and replace the flooring/sub-floor.

requirements_title: 16390786  - SECTOR NORTHERN NEW ENGLAND Repair Exterior Buildings 1, 2, and 5 Sector NNE (FY27)
requirement:
Repair Exterior Buildings 1, 2, and 5 Sector Northern New England. Repair /replace siding, roof, ex.t man doors, OH doors and windows. Incudes gutters, downspouts and snowguards.  Major M&R of these buildings include:

• Window caulking repair
• Masonry repairs
• ADA Ramp/Railings repair
• Concrete walkway/stairway repairs
• Replace Doors
• Repair foundation/water infiltration
• Abate deteriorated LBP in boiler room
• Minor roof repairs

BACKGROUND: Buildings 1 & 2 are masonry exterior structures that were building approximately 100 years ago.  Both buildings are aging and need repairs to extend operational readiness for the Sector personnel.

The exterior masonry requires re-pointing and repairs to ensure a weathertight envelope.  In addition the windows and doors are leaking during adverse weather and require repair/reseal.  This is causing damages to finished occupied spaces within the buildings.

The concrete foundation is cracking and water is infiltrating into the mechanical/electrical spaces. requirement:
The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) requires an innovative, long-term solution to manage contaminated environmental media at Base Kodiak, Alaska. This program aims to drastically reduce the generation of soil spoils from construction activities and to develop a permanent facility capable of treating contaminated soil.

This Scope of Work (SOW) outlines a multi-phased design-build project. The contractor shall provide a complete solution encompassing initial feasibility studies for soil reduction, pilot-scale testing of advanced treatment technologies, and the final design and installation of a contaminated media segregation pad and permanent soil management facility.  The objective is to develop an integrated soil management system with capabilities to perform onsite soil treatment. An assessment of available treatment technologies shall be conducted with an onsite pilot test determining the effectiveness of treating listed contaminants. There will likely be more than one treatment technology needed to treat contaminants of concern (COCs).

These projects range across multiple disciplines, including mechanical, electrical, civil, structural, architectural, and life-safety, and include, but are not limited to, HVAC and roofing repairs/replacements, interior and exterior facility repairs, ATFP security upgrades, C5I system upgrades, and utility infrastructure modernization. Coordination between all projects is necessary.

Inspection services will span the entire construction duration, estimated at approximately 36 months, from pre-construction services and site preparation, through equipment installation, and ultimately to commissioning, closeout, and acceptance. These measures range across multiple disciplines, electrical, mechanical, civil, and utility infrastructure, and include boiler and steam system upgrades, building envelope improvements, electrical distribution enhancements, and process system upgrades. Coordination between all projects is necessary. Construction inspection requirements for this project include labor, material, equipment, mobilization, demobilization, quality control services and ancillary items required to oversee and verify construction progress for the new and upgraded facilities and infrastructure improvements. The objectives at LORAN Station Yap are to perform a supplemental Remedial Investigation (RI) following the recommendations detailed in the December 2025 RI Report. This will be accomplished through the following actions:

1.	Removal of 400cy of lead and PCB contaminated soils from specific DUs and DAs in Area A. This will be followed by confirmation sampling.
2.	Multi-Increment sampling of sediment from specific DUs in Landfill-1 to track the anticipated decline of PCB concentrations. 
3.	Biota sampling from both inside and outside the Maakiy Causeway to track the anticipated decline of PCB concentrations.
4.	Inspect and remove debris that was marked and left during the last investigation.
